title: Flatness of polynomial local prefix quotients passes from finite coefficient subrings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $R_0\subseteq R$ a finite type integer subring [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Fix $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], a prime ideal $Q$ of $R[x]$, and an integer $i\geq0$. For every finite type integer subring $B$ containing $R_0$, put $Q_B=Q\cap B[x]$ and let $f_{j,B}$ be the coefficientwise image of $f_j$. Suppose $B[x]_{Q_B}/(f_{1,B},\ldots,f_{\min(i,c),B})$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat over $B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $R[x]_Q/(f_{1,R},\ldots,f_{\min(i,c),R})$ is flat over $R$. No complete-intersection, equation-containment or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Index by the finite type integer subrings B of R containing R0. This is nonempty because R0 is a stage, directed because the union of finite sets of ring generators generates a common stage, and covers R because any requested element can be adjoined to generators of R0. Contract Q to every polynomial subring. Inclusions preserve the contracted-prime complements, so localization gives compatible ring maps; these send each equation to its next-stage image and descend to the prefix quotients. The induced maps are linear over the source-stage subring and obey identity, composition and compatibility with the full quotient.

Every class in the full quotient is represented by a fraction h/s, with s outside Q. Adjoining all coefficients of h and s to a finite generating set of R0 gives a finite type stage containing that fraction, proving the representation condition of the directed-union flat-module theorem.

If a stage class h/s maps to zero in the full quotient, membership in the ideal generated by the finite prefix gives a sum of polynomial fractions times those equations. Choose a common denominator t outside Q; equality of fractions supplies u outside Q with u*(t*h - s*sum_j a_j*f_j)=0 in R[x]. Enlarge the stage by the finitely many coefficients of t,u and the a_j. Its polynomial inclusion into R[x] is injective, so the identity holds in the enlarged stage. The denominators remain outside its contracted prime, and this identity makes the original class vanish there. This proves eventual vanishing.

Apply the directed-union-subrings flat-module theorem with these stage quotients and maps. The first step gives the directed cover and all compatibility conditions, the next two steps give representation and eventual vanishing, and hstage is flatness at every stage. The resulting flat module is exactly the specified full polynomial local prefix quotient. Empty prefixes, prefixes longer than the list and zero quotients satisfy the same argument.

theorem flat_polynomial_local_quotient_of_finiteType_subrings
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (R₀ : Subring R)
    (hR₀ : Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀) {n c : ℕ}
    (f₀ : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R₀)
    (Q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) [Q.IsPrime] (i : ℕ)
    (hstage : ∀ (B : Subring R) (hB : R₀ ≤ B), Algebra.FiniteType ℤ B →
      Module.Flat B
        (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (MvPolynomial.map B.subtype)) ⧸
          Ideal.ofList (((List.ofFn
            (fun j ↦ MvPolynomial.map (Subring.inclusion hB) (f₀ j))).map
              (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) B)
                (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (MvPolynomial.map B.subtype))))).take i))) :
    Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime Q ⧸
      Ideal.ofList (((List.ofFn (fun j ↦ MvPolynomial.map R₀.subtype (f₀ j))).map
        (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.AtPrime Q))).take i))
